card.occupation: Pharmacy technician, working three and a half days a week (about 26 hours) at an independent community pharmacy in Leyton. She does dispensing accuracy checks, medicines reconciliation for care home patients and supervises the two counter assistants.
card.education_detail: BSc in Pharmacy from a university in Manila. She came to the UK at 22 and couldn't afford the conversion route to register as a pharmacist, so she did an NVQ Level 3 in Pharmaceutical Science through work and registered with the GPhC as a technician in her late twenties. Since then she has done a short accredited course in accuracy checking.
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom Victorian terrace flat with her partner of nine years, Daniel, 43, a freelance sound engineer who works on corporate events and some theatre. They're not married and talk about it now and then without much urgency. They have no children and a rescue cat called Mango. The second bedroom is half office, half Daniel's equipment.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Quezon City, Philippines. Roman Catholic upbringing; she still goes to Mass at a Filipino-heavy parish in East London maybe twice a month and always at Christmas and Easter, partly for faith and partly for the community and the food afterwards. Her mum and younger brother are still in Manila and she sends money home monthly. She has a British passport now. She feels at home in London but is quietly sensitive about having 'downgraded' professionally by moving.
card.professional_persona: Precise and quick at the bench, and good with anxious elderly patients because she can tell when they're worried. She privately thinks she knows more than some of the locum pharmacists and occasionally lets that show. She is careful about how she comes across to the owner and makes sure he notices when she's covered extra. She dislikes conflict with customers and goes over a rude exchange for the rest of the day.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, mostly round the Walthamstow Wetlands and Lloyd Park, and did a beginners' yoga block at a studio on Hoe Street that she keeps meaning to restart. She'll watch the Olympics gymnastics but couldn't name a footballer beyond the obvious ones.
card.arts_persona: This is where she comes alive. She does a weekly evening wheel-throwing pottery class and sells the odd mug on Instagram. She goes to the William Morris Gallery, which is round the corner, and to the Tate Modern or small East London gallery openings, often on her own. She reads literary fiction, a lot of it translated, and likes melancholy films. She is quite proud of her taste and a bit dismissive of things she finds 'basic'.
card.travel_persona: Flies to Manila every other year, usually for a month, and finds it emotionally draining as much as lovely. With Daniel she prefers city breaks with museums and good coffee, such as Lisbon, Copenhagen and Kyoto (once, saved up for ages). She gets very anxious about flights and connections and over-plans. She likes nicer hotels than they can really afford.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks Filipino food when homesick: sinigang, adobo, pancit for birthdays. Otherwise it's whatever she's seen on social media that week. Daniel does most of the weeknight dinners. She loves trying new restaurants and is a bit of a food snob about 'proper' versus 'Instagram' places, though she still photographs her plate.
skills: making a small budget look stylish
card.career_goals: She'd like a better-paid technician role, possibly in a hospital or a GP practice pharmacy team, but she keeps the part-time hours for the pottery and her own sanity. She half-seriously wants the pottery to become a proper side income with a market stall and a web shop. She sometimes still resents not being a pharmacist and has looked at the overseas pharmacist route more than once.
card.voice: Soft, fairly quiet, mid-pace, slowing down when she's thinking. Her accent is Filipino-English that has been rounded off by eighteen years in London; vowels are mostly London now, with a slight Filipino rhythm. She says 'erm' a lot at the start of answers and uses 'sort of' and 'you know' as softeners. When she's relaxed she sometimes adds 'honestly' or 'to be fair'. She calls the evening meal dinner, says knackered, and calls Daniel 'my partner' to strangers. She doesn't rush to fill a silence and will let it sit while she thinks, then answer fairly fully. If she's misunderstood she'll say 'sorry, no, I mean...' and rephrase. She gets livelier and quicker on art or food.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase for quick answers but capitalises names and 'I' properly. She uses apostrophes correctly because she's slightly particular about it. She uses commas more than full stops, and sometimes ends with 'x' out of habit then deletes it. She writes the occasional 'tbh' or 'idk' and no emojis in forms.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite at first, a bit watchful, a little hard to read. She answers what's asked without volunteering much until she senses the other person is genuinely interested, especially in something she cares about. She can come across as slightly aloof or as if she's quietly judging, and sometimes she is. She warms up noticeably if complimented on something she made or chose.
small_things: her cat knocking a plant off the windowsill
a glaze that came out a completely different colour from the test tile
a new bakery on Hoe Street that's overpriced but good
being knackered after a Saturday shift
repeat prescription chaos before bank holidays
what she's reading at the moment
deeper_things: feeling she wasted her pharmacy degree, and some embarrassment telling people back home what she does
guilt about how often she visits her mum, who is getting older
worrying about money because Daniel's freelance income is up and down
mixed feelings about marriage and the fact that her family keeps asking
anxiety spells, mostly before travel or after confrontations at work, that she's never seen a GP about
a sense that her Catholic faith is more about belonging now than belief
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly off-centre, showing her from mid-chest up. Daylight comes from a window to her left, so the right side of her face is a little shadowed. She has a round face, light brown skin, dark brown eyes and a small polite closed-mouth smile that looks a bit guarded. Her straight black shoulder-length hair is tucked behind one ear. She wears thin tortoiseshell rectangular glasses, a mustard-yellow ribbed jumper and small gold hoop earrings. Behind her is a white painted wall with a wooden shelf holding three handmade mugs in speckled blue and cream glazes, a trailing pothos and a stack of paperbacks. Partly visible in the right of the frame is a framed William Morris print of willow leaves. In the bottom corner is the edge of a grey sofa with a mustard cushion.
